evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep says 'I'll ask you few questions in order for us to build you a code wherein you can depend on this would take within the next five to ten minutes of your time. Would that be okay?' — time-boxed and dependable quote framing present, but 'five to ten minutes' deviates from script's '10 to 15 minutes' and customer answers 'Okay, sure' so waits for yes.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Rep asks: 'before we proceed, I just wanted to check do you have any concerns or any important things that you wanted to answer during this call today?' Asked early, before logistics probing begins.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raises concern about heavy bedroom furniture on second floor with no elevator. Rep acknowledges ('Yeah. No worries we can definitely take note of that'), asks clarifying follow-up ('And, and that was only for like, two flights upstairs. We're just only like one flight of stairs.'), customer corrects ('It's just one. Yeah'), rep confirms understanding ('Oh, just two stories. Okay'). This is two-layer depth on the stated concern.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: Rep does not reflect back a summary like 'So what I'm hearing is ___, ___, and ___. Did I get all of it?' No reflection provided.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Rep gathers: property type (storage unit, then apartment), floor/stories (second floor storage, second floor apartment), number of rooms (one bedroom), walking distance (minute walk from storage unit, stairs right there at apartment), additional rooms (none mentioned, customer notes no kitchen/living room furniture yet), special considerations (heavy dressers, no elevator), storage size (10x13). All seven items covered.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Rep never asks 'Would you like us to pack your items into boxes for you?' Not offered.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Rep asks 'How many boxes do you have here?' Customer says 'It's like everything should fit in a bedroom. Basically. It's one bedroom.' Rep follows with 'Is it full?' — the box count check is asked.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep provides: 'a typical one bedroom apartment would normally takes two movers between two and a half to three and a half hours' (anchor). Personalizes to this move: 'in your case we're coming from a storage unit going to the new location which is like, ten minutes away from the first location so which is located on the second floor with stairs we'll send out two reviews on one truck estimated time is between three to four hours estimated cost would be $832' (personalized to specifics of move and concern about heavy items/stairs).
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Rep delivers: trip fee/fees transparency: 'Only thing that is outside of our early weight is non because this is within our free travel zone' and 'there's no hidden fees of any type. No credit card fees, no sterle. Fees, no disassemble or reassembly fees.' And minimum/increments: 'We have a minimum of two and a half hours once you go over that it will always be prorated into fifteen minute increments.' Both present.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Rep never asks 'Does that feel fair?' or similar. After giving the estimate ($832, 3-4 hours), immediately pivots to availability: 'And I just wanted to let you know that we can be able to book her slot on Thursday.' No pause or check-in on the estimate itself.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Rep states: 'Finally we have on time guarantee we value your time. So, if you cannot make it to the time window that we arrange we immediately start discounting money of your final bill.' Covers discount terms (immediately starts discounting if late) in recognizable form.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Rep states: 'So first is that we have no worry damage coverage included on the already weight that. We are that you're paying us. We will provide up to $2,000 per move that is to repair replace and reimburse for your items.' Covers $2,000 coverage and that it's included (built into rate). Does not explicitly state 'no deductible / no fine print' framing.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: Rep does not ask 'Does that put those to rest?' or similar to confirm the Two Promises are settled. Instead moves straight to booking availability.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Rep does not ask 'What's still concerning you about this move?' or genuine final concerns check. Jumps to booking logistics without a final concern check.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Rep never asks 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' or equivalent catch-all.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Rep asks: 'Would you like our help with your move?' Asked plainly, no built-in out provided. Customer responds 'Yes.'
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Rep states: 'There's no deposit required, no recent securing your spot.' No explicit rate-lock framing ('your quote is locked in' or similar), but confirms no deposit needed.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Rep confirms: date (Thursday, October 1st), time (9:00 AM), phone number (captured earlier), addresses (both confirmed), unit number (201), apartment details (second floor). Rep says 'I'll send you confirmation email' and reviews what will be in it. All booking details confirmed; notes for crew about concern (heavy furniture) are mentioned implicitly via 'It will go over absolutely everything that we talk about' but not explicitly called out as crew notes left.

top_strength: Rep asked the customer's concerns early (before probing), then followed up two layers deep on the specific worry about heavy furniture on stairs, and successfully gathered all seven logistics details needed for an accurate estimate.
coaching_note: Add a genuine final concerns check ('What's still concerning you?') before the ask, and ask 'Does that feel fair?' after the estimate to create a real pause for customer processing instead of moving immediately into availability.
